html:
A drive by Qing China from 1861 to 1895 to adopt Western weapons, ships and industry while keeping its Confucian system of rule. Its slogan, later put in words by the official Zhang Zhidong, was "Chinese learning for the essence, Western learning for use".

It began after defeat in the Second Opium War and amid the Taiping Rebellion. Prince Gong at court and provincial leaders such as Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang led it.

  • A foreign office, the Zongli Yamen, opened in 1861.
  • Arsenals and shipyards were built at Shanghai and Fuzhou.
  • Schools trained translators, and students went abroad.
  • Companies for shipping, mining, telegraphs and textiles were founded.

Results were real but patchy. Projects depended on a few officials, money was short, and the court, under Cixi, was cautious. China lost a war with France in 1884 to 1885. In the war with Japan of 1894 to 1895 the new northern fleet was destroyed. Japan's deeper reforms after the Meiji Restoration had worked far better.
